object_description: curved five-armed building volume in a park landscape
design_condition: The centrally positioned, five-armed volume is embedded in the park and interweaves open space across the plot, while its constant roof edge makes it appear particularly high where the surrounding terrain slopes downward.

positive.statement: The independent stance strengthens the essential characteristics of the protected townscape.
The curved volume creates an interesting interweaving of open space across the plot boundaries.
The building is cleverly perceived as a collection of smaller volumes within the green urban body.
The public permeability of the ground floor and the spaciousness of the reception area are particularly welcomed.
The garden pockets, entrance and small campus create pleasantly different atmospheres and respectfully engage the existing buildings.
The existing trees are integrated into the overall concept with a high degree of sensitivity.
The architectural expression supports the curved form and is appropriate and largely understandable.
The vertical pilaster layer creates permeability, intimacy and structural sun protection.
The low-invasive conversion of the existing building appears precise and well thought out.
The intensive green roof makes a valuable contribution to biodiversity.
The proposal is robust in terms of building physics and construction.

negative.statement: The constant roof edge makes the volumes appear particularly high compared with the surrounding street.
The longer facade development causes the project to lose economic efficiency.
The arrangement of the treatment rooms was assessed very critically because privacy can hardly be guaranteed.
The waiting areas remain separated from the facade, limiting views to the outside.
The corridors on the facade are questioned at the laboratory level.
The long walk between the office pool and laboratories is impractical and undesirable.
The future viability of such a specific form was controversially discussed.
The curved shape creates many narrow, angled spaces that are critical for use.
The insulation standard on the inner-courtyard facades must be increased, and functional summer thermal protection is lacking.
